sources.entry: Activepieces - No-code business automation tool like Zapier or Tray. For example, you can send a Slack notification for each new Trello card. (Source Code) MIT Docker
Activepieces | No-code workflow automation with hundreds of integrations, a Zapier alternative

summary.one_liner: Activepieces is an open-source, self-hostable no-code automation platform (a Zapier alternative) whose integrations, called pieces, are written in TypeScript.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a no-code workflow builder for business automation, with flows built from pieces (integrations) such as Google Sheets, OpenAI, Discord and RSS, and it says there are 200+ or 280+ pieces depending on the section. Builder features listed include loops, branches, automatic retries, HTTP requests, code steps with NPM packages, an AI-assisted code piece, fully versioned flows, translations and customizable templates. Pieces are TypeScript npm packages with hot reloading for local development, and the README states they are automatically available as MCP servers for use with Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf. Human-in-the-loop pieces (delays and approvals) and human input triggers (chat and form interfaces) are also described. The Community Edition is MIT-licensed, while enterprise features fall under a commercial license.
use_cases: connect Google Sheets, Discord or RSS to other apps without coding
build AI agents and LLM-assisted data cleanup flows
expose integrations as MCP tools for Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf
add approval or delay steps to automated workflows
create chat or form triggers for workflows
develop custom TypeScript integrations (pieces) for internal services
how_to_run: Self-hosting instructions are referenced in the README but the commands are not included in the text provided.
See the Documentation and Contributor's Guide linked from the README for setup and piece development.
notable: Pieces are TypeScript npm packages with hot reloading for local development
Pieces are exposed as MCP servers for LLM clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor and Windsurf
Over 200 integrations, with about 60% contributed by the community, according to the README
Built-in human-in-the-loop approval and delay steps, plus chat and form input triggers
caveats: Enterprise features are under a commercial license rather than MIT
The README text provided contains no explicit Docker or install commands, so setup details must come from the linked documentation
summary.license: MIT (Community Edition; enterprise features under Commercial License)
